The 'privatelink' section was added later and carries its own pulled date: the top-level 'pulled' above covers fargate and bedrock only.

bedrock.note_region: This model is NOT offered in eu-central-1 at all (checked: no eu-central-1 rows exist in the Price List API for it) -- the 'us.' prefix in MODEL_ID is a cross-region inference profile, meaning a real (non-stubbed) call would leave eu-central-1 and bill against US-region rates below. This is a real architectural fact about the current deployment, not a rate-card footnote: Bedrock traffic for this exact MODEL_ID cannot stay in-region.

privatelink.note: Pulled 2026-09-22, thirteen days after the rest of this file, which is why it carries its own date -- the top-level 'pulled' does not describe this section. Only the first tier is reachable at this workload: report 4.5's reference month moves 8.6 GB, five orders of magnitude below the 1 PB boundary, so the cheaper tiers are recorded for completeness and never apply. Cross-check: the same product family prices EUC1-VpcEndpoint-Hours at $0.012/h, which is endpoint_eni_hour (FR14) as read independently from CUR -- two sources agreeing on the neighbouring rate.
